claims.text: High-temperature structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys is governed by the formation of stable, coherent interfaces between nanoalloy grains.
Stable, coherent interfaces act as barriers to grain growth.
Stable, coherent interfaces inhibit chemical degradation.
Heating high-entropy nanoalloys to high temperature promotes the formation or persistence of coherent interfaces between grains.
High-entropy nanoalloys possessing coherent grain interfaces will exhibit less grain growth at high temperature than an unstable baseline nanoalloy.
High-entropy nanoalloys possessing coherent grain interfaces will exhibit less chemical degradation at high temperature than an unstable baseline nanoalloy.
The prediction is intended to apply from 500°C to 1000°C.
The prediction is intended to apply to grain sizes from 10 nm to 100 nm.
An unstable nanoalloy baseline undergoes grain growth at high temperature.
An unstable nanoalloy baseline undergoes chemical degradation at high temperature.
